actions.change: kmod 33: add `--disable-manpages` to the recipe configure, so the absent scdoc man-page builder no longer stops configure

openvpn: pin the 2.5 line (2.5.10) and configure `--with-crypto-library=openssl --disable-lzo --disable-lz4 --disable-plugin-auth-pam`, because 2.6.12 requires libnl-genl-3.0 (DCO) and then libcap-ng on Linux, neither admitted here
isync: add `-Wl,-rpath-link,{prefix}/lib` to the link environment so libssl's transitive libcrypto dependency resolves against the authority prefix

libssh 0.10.6 ships only CMakeLists.txt and the venue still admits no cmake, so both the authority and the candidate stop at L1-admitted-source with `cmake configure failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'cmake'`. The re-measurement re-labels the family `authority-baseline-limited` because the authority fails identically at the same rung; that is a class transition, not a repair, and the family is still blocked below L4-linked and is recorded still-blocked rather than faked
actions.evidence: forensics/downstream/p1000-run.json verdict:p1000:libssh (authority and candidate both L1-admitted-source, DROP_IN_NOT_APPLICABLE, configure fails for the absent cmake); tarball inspection: libssh-0.10.6.tar.xz root has CMakeLists.txt and no configure

actions.change: lighttpd 1.4.76's release tarball ships configure.ac but no generated ./configure; the recipe now bootstraps it with the pinned bookworm autotools, takes PCRE2 from its pinned package seam, and builds LIGHTTPD_STATIC=yes so mod_openssl is compiled into `src/lighttpd`, leaving the source tree pristine. The re-measured verdict is DROP_IN_PASS at L7-functional for both subjects, so the family is no longer blocked

pure-ftpd: add a deterministic local authenticated FTPS workload -- a system account the venue creates in its disposable container, driven over explicit TLS by the authority's own `openssl s_client -starttls ftp` (USER/PASS/PWD) on loopback
isync: add a deterministic local IMAP4rev1-over-TLS peer (served by the courtroom over the authority-generated certificate on loopback) that the subject mbsync syncs a message from into a Maildir
admit a bounded, deterministic batch of recipe-less counted families whose pinned release tarball ships a build entry point the venue can execute and needs no missing tool (see `new_recipes`)

before.captured_note: the pre-remediation 24.16 blocker partition, captured once before the planes were re-measured and committed as the record's `before`

non_claims: a bounded, deterministic admission batch is not an attempt at all 988 recipe-less families: it is the subset this subphase built and measured, and it makes no claim about the rest
a build/link is not a functional proof: a newly-admitted family that reached L4-linked has compiled and linked, not behaved, and one with no admitted local workload is `no-fixture`

a still-blocked class is a measurement of the fixed venue, not of the project: libssh needs cmake, which this venue does not admit (its authority and candidate both stop at L1-admitted-source); lighttpd's absent generated configure is a recipe gap the pinned-toolchain recipe closes, so its L7-functional/DROP_IN_PASS is a recipe fix and not a project claim
the before figures are a preserved measurement of the pre-remediation planes, recorded once and carried forward like 24.11's holdout first_run, not re-derived from planes that no longer exist
a deterministic local fixture is one exercise of the program's OpenSSL path on loopback, not a statement that every consumer works or that the library is safe

rule.actions: the exact recipe/flag/fixture each repair applied, with the family it targets and the class it names; a resolving action must show its named families reached the resolving class (`none`, DROP_IN_PASS) in the re-measured planes, and a still-blocked action must show none of them did, cite the rung the family stopped at, and name the missing tool
rule.admission_criterion: a recipe is admissible when its pinned release tarball ships a build entry point the venue can execute (a generated `configure`, or a plain `Makefile`) and needs no tool the venue lacks; the batch is bounded and deterministic, and the candidates the venue could not build are recorded with the reason
rule.after: the blocker partition re-derived from the committed (re-measured) Phase-24 planes through 24.16's own code path, so the record cannot drift from the analysis
rule.before: the 24.16 blocker partition of the pre-remediation planes, captured once (before the re-measurement) and committed as `forensics/downstream/blocker-remediation-baseline.json`; the planes it measured are superseded by the re-measurement, so it is a preserved measured input rather than a re-derivation from planes that no longer exist
honesty_labels: a bounded admission batch is not an attempt at all 988 recipe-less families
a build/link is not a functional proof
a still-blocked class is a measurement of the fixed venue, not of the project
rule.movement: the per-class difference between `after` and `before`, computed as a subtraction of two measured class counts, plus the per-family class transitions
rule.name: the biggest-mover remediation record
